summary: The code is syntactically valid but does not implement the required multi-agent simulation. main() is empty and, due to an unterminated class docstring, the direct call to main() is inside a string and will not execute. Key entities and the simulation loop, calibration, and metrics are missing. Some logic issues exist (e.g., Watts–Strogatz k parity).

issues.description: No simulation is implemented. main() is empty; there is no orchestration of data loading, agent creation, network construction, simulation loop (days 0–39), or prediction (days 30–39). No evaluation metrics are computed.
issues.solution: Implement the end-to-end pipeline: load/synthesize data, initialize agents and network, run daily simulation (information diffusion, risk updates, mask decisions, purchases, policy effects) for 40 days, store mask-wearing time series, compute metrics (including RMSE) for the prediction window.

issues.description: The direct call to main() is inside an unterminated triple-quoted string (class Location docstring), so it will not execute. This violates the requirement to call main() at global scope.
issues.location: End of file: class Location docstring and the main() call
issues.solution:
Close the class Location docstring properly and ensure the main() call is outside any string literal. For example:

@dataclass
class Location:
    """..."""
    id: int
    # add fields...
    pass

# Execute main for both direct execution and sandbox wrapper invocation
main()

issues.description: Core entities are missing or incomplete: Location is truncated and has no fields; Retailer, PublicHealthAuthority, and InformationChannel classes are not defined but referenced in behaviors.
issues.location: Entities section: Person references Retailer; Location class stub
issues.solution: Define classes for Location, Retailer, PublicHealthAuthority, and InformationChannel with attributes and behaviors as specified. Ensure Person.purchase_masks and policy/media interactions have concrete counterparts to call.

issues.description: Evaluation metrics, particularly RMSE over the prediction window (days 30–39), are not computed.
issues.solution: After running the simulation, aggregate predicted mask-wearing rates and compare to actuals (if available) using RMSE. Also compute the specified descriptive metrics (overall adoption, peak, sustained, inequality, noncompliance, availability, estimated transmission reduction).

issues.description: Watts–Strogatz graph parameter k must be even, but the synthesis logic adjusts k to an odd value, likely causing exceptions and fallback to random edges.
issues.solution: Ensure k is even: use k_even = k if k % 2 == 0 else k + 1 (bounded by N-1 and at least 2).

issues.description: Policy activation and enforcement mechanisms are not integrated into a simulation loop; Person.comply_with_policy exists but is never invoked within interactions/locations.
issues.location: No simulation loop invoking comply_with_policy or location interactions
issues.solution: Implement daily interactions by location type, apply mask requirements and enforcement probabilities, and update noncompliance_rate metrics.

issues.description: Information diffusion is partially implemented at the agent level but lacks global messaging/media channels and neighbor info computation per layer.
issues.location: Person.share_information is present, but no caller or network aggregation
issues.solution: At each time step, compute neighbor info shares per layer, invoke share_information for all agents, and incorporate InformationChannel/PublicHealthAuthority messaging with credibility and intensity.

issues.description: Retail mask stock and pricing dynamics are not implemented, despite references in Person.purchase_masks and parameters.
issues.location: Missing Retailer class; purchase_masks cannot function
issues.solution: Implement Retailer with stock_level, restock_rate, price_per_mask, supply_reliability, and methods sell_masks, restock, update_price. Track mask_availability metric.

issues.description: Person.share_information uses epsilon_info as a spontaneous adoption probability. The naming suggests decay/noise; the semantics should be clarified to avoid double draws against p_info and epsilon.
issues.solution: Use a single Bernoulli draw with combined probability or explicitly document epsilon_info as exogenous seeding. Optionally separate retention/decay and seeding steps deterministically.

issues.description: Multiple functions retain a 'pass' statement before actual logic, which is redundant.
issues.location: logistic, clip01, poisson, ConfigManager.__init__, get_param, get_prediction_period, get_evaluation_metrics, DataLoader methods, Person methods
issues.solution: Remove redundant pass statements to improve clarity.
